name: message-scroller
title: Message Scroller
description: The scrolling list of a conversation, which follows new content only while the reader is following along. Wrap `Message` elements with stable keys in `MessageScroller` and give it a height. It starts at the latest message. While the reader is at the bottom, new messages and streaming growth stay in view. The moment they scroll up, it stops following, nothing moves under them, and a 'Jump to latest' pill appears, counting messages that arrived meanwhile ('2 new messages'). Clicking it scrolls smoothly back down and pins again. When older messages load above (`onReachTop` fires near the top), the view compensates for the added height, so the page doesn't jump. Screen readers hear `announcement`, which you set when a message finishes, never per token. The region is keyboard-scrollable and named 'Conversation'. Use it for any chat or agent transcript. Not for feeds that should always show the newest item first.
docs: Requires `cn` at `@/lib/utils`. Give children stable `key`s, because history prepends are detected by the first key changing. Give the scroller a height (`h-[…]` or `flex-1` in a flex column). Set `announcement` when a reply finishes.

meta.engineeringNotes: Auto-scroll is where chat interfaces most often break trust: a stream drags the view down while someone is reading an earlier answer. Here 'pinned' is a fact about the reader, recomputed from their own scroll position with a 48px tolerance. Following happens only while pinned, both when children are added (layout effect) and when the last message grows during streaming (a ResizeObserver on the content, since token growth adds no children). While unpinned, added children are counted into the jump pill. A smooth jump sets a guard, so the intermediate 'not at bottom' frames of the animation don't unpin and flash the pill back. A 700ms fallback lands on the bottom even if streaming moved the target mid-animation. Prepended history is detected by the first child's key changing alongside a higher count, and compensated by adding the height delta to scrollTop in a layout effect before paint. Native `overflow-anchor` is disabled, so browsers with and without support behave identically. Accessibility uses a named, focusable region for keyboard scrolling and a separate polite status for caller-supplied announcements, because a live log would read every streamed token.
meta.motionNotes: Following while pinned is instant, not smooth: animating toward a target that moves with every token lags behind and reads as sluggish. Smooth scrolling is reserved for the user's explicit 'Jump to latest', and falls back to instant under prefers-reduced-motion. The jump pill fades in at `--pd-duration-fast` on the decelerate curve when the reader leaves the bottom, and hover colour runs at `--pd-duration-instant`. History prepends are compensated before paint, so there is no visible jump. Everything becomes instant under prefers-reduced-motion.
